nin-zdrijac.description: The old town of Nin, 15 km from Zadar, is surrounded by shallow sandy beaches and a lagoon — Croatia's main kite area for learning. In summer the Maestral blows from the northwest in the afternoon, and the water stays waist-deep far from shore. A dozen more spots nearby (Sabunike, Privlaka, Vir, Šimuni on Pag) work in different wind directions.
nin-zdrijac.rating_basis: Northern Dalmatia's most popular kite area: shallow water and sandy beaches around Nin, several schools (kitejungle lists dozens of spots in the Nin–Pag–Privlaka area)
nin-zdrijac.waves_note: Shallow sandy bay at Nin: flat water and light chop in the Maestral; waves only in a strong Jugo
nin-zdrijac.hazards: Swimmers and swimming zones in summer; in a Bora the wind is offshore and very gusty
nin-zdrijac.gustiness_note: The summer Maestral is a steady daytime thermal; the winter Bora is very gusty and offshore
nin-zdrijac.crowd_note: Lots of students and holidaymakers on the beaches around Nin in summer
pros: Zadar airport and plenty of accommodation nearby
cons: Summer wind is moderate and not daily
Crowded in July–August
The winter Bora is offshore and dangerous
nin-zdrijac.wind_dir: NW (Maestral), side-onshore; in winter Bora (NE) and Jugo (SE)

viganj-peljesac.description: A small village on the south coast of the Pelješac peninsula, opposite Korčula — a classic Croatian wind spot. The summer Maestral accelerates in the narrow channel and blows along the shore in the afternoon. There's a dedicated kite beach, campsites and stations; the water is deep and choppy, so the spot is better suited to confident riders.
viganj-peljesac.rating_basis: Kite-and-windsurfing-guide puts Viganj alongside Bol and Perna as thermal spots with up to 5 Bft in the channel; a long-established windsurf spot with a dedicated kite beach and campsites
viganj-peljesac.waves_note: The channel between Pelješac and Korčula: chop, practically no waves
viganj-peljesac.hazards: Windsurfers and boats in the channel, the Orebić–Korčula ferry route nearby; deep water
viganj-peljesac.gustiness_note: The summer thermal is accelerated by the Venturi effect in the 1.5 km Pelješac–Korčula channel to ~5 Bft; it blows in the second half of the day
viganj-peljesac.crowd_note: Lots of windsurfers and kiters in the narrow channel in summer, but fewer than at Bol
cons: Deep water — not the best place for first lessons
Wind only in the second half of the day, and moderate
A long journey (ferry or the road along Pelješac)
viganj-peljesac.wind_dir: W–NW (thermal Maestral), side-shore along the channel
viganj-peljesac.airport: DBV — Dubrovnik, ~2 h; SPU — Split, ~3 h

bali-sanur.description: Sanur is a laid-back resort on Bali's southeast coast where the southeast trade wind blows from June to September. A barrier reef forms a flat-water lagoon — a handy place to learn — and the outer reef sometimes has waves. Riding depends on the tide: at low tide the lagoon is too shallow.
bali-sanur.rating_basis: Bali's main kite spot: a regular trade wind in the dry season and a lagoon behind the reef, but riding depends heavily on the tide and the wind is moderate — more a convenient place to learn and holiday than a top destination
bali-sanur.waves_note: Between the beach and the barrier reef (~0.5–1 km) lies a flat-water lagoon with chop at high tide; the outer reef has waves for experienced wave riders
bali-sanur.hazards: Shallow reef and coral at low tide (wear booties), sea urchins, currents in the reef passes, speedboats to Nusa Penida and Lembongan, waves on the outer reef
bali-sanur.gustiness_note: Dry season, trade wind from June to September; the wind is fairly steady and builds towards midday; riding is mostly possible at mid and high tide
bali-sanur.crowd_note: The lagoon gets busy in July–August: schools, SUP, boats to Nusa Penida
pros: Trade wind June–September, when the season in Thailand and Vietnam is weak
Bali's well-developed infrastructure, easy to combine with surfing and a holiday
cons: Riding only at mid/high tide
Moderate wind, sometimes underpowered
November to March is the rainy season with almost no wind
Boat traffic

sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.description: Mallasoro in South Sulawesi is a little-known but very windy Indonesian lagoon: from April to October the southeast trade wind blows almost daily from morning to sunset. The shallow sandy lagoon, over 2 km long, with flat clear water suits both learning and freestyle. An alternative to Bali in the same season, but with much stronger and steadier wind.
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: wind 80–100% of the time from April to October, a 2 km shallow flat lagoon for every level and for big air, far from the crowds; downsides — a single place to stay and basic infrastructure
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.waves_note: A sandy lagoon over 2 km long: shallow, flat, clear water, small kickers at high tide, glassy at low tide; no waves and no shorebreak
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.hazards: Far from medical care, strong sun, shallows at low tide; the guide names no specific hazards
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.gustiness_note: In season the wind blows from morning to evening — 80–100% of the time according to IKSURFMAG, 20–35 kn at peak
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.crowd_note: Practically deserted — there's one place to stay at the spot, and it's mostly its guests who ride
sulawesi-jeneponto-mallasoro.region: South Sulawesi, Jeneponto Regency, Mallasoro village, ~80 km from Makassar
pros: Very steady, strong trade wind April–October
Inexpensive: meals $3–4, accommodation at the spot ~$60/night
cons: One place to stay at the spot, little entertainment
Weak internet (3G)
You have to fly to Makassar and drive 1.5–2 h
November–March is the rainy season with no wind

rameswaram-dhanushkodi.description: Pamban Island between India and Sri Lanka is India's main kite region. The long spit leading to the abandoned town of Dhanushkodi is washed by Palk Bay on one side and the Gulf of Mannar on the other, so in almost any wind you'll find a flat lagoon or a reef wave. The southwest monsoon season runs April–September, the northerly wind season December–March.
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG calls Rameswaram a “paradise” for beginners and advanced riders alike: two wind seasons, flat lagoons and reef waves, only a handful of kiters on the water; downsides — remoteness and the need for permits
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.waves_note: Sheltered bays and flat-water lagoons (the islands act as a breakwater); waves on the reefs, especially before and after the monsoon
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.hazards: Reefs, remoteness (rescue only by the school), border zone and bans on kiting without a permit; rain and cyclone season October–December
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.gustiness_note: Two seasons of 4–5 months each: southwest monsoon 18–25 kn, northerly winter wind 15–20 kn; steady ocean wind
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.crowd_note: Only a handful of kiters; the main spot sees almost no tourists or fishermen
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.region: Tamil Nadu, Pamban Island (Rameswaram), Dhanushkodi spit
pros: Two wind seasons — almost all year except October–November
Flat lagoons and reef waves close together
cons: Kiting requires permits — in practice only through a local school
Few schools and rentals, basic accommodation
Remote: ~2 h from Madurai airport
Very hot in May–June
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.wind_dir: SW (April–September), N–NE (December–March); the island lets you pick a shore for any direction, cross-shore at the main spot
rameswaram-dhanushkodi.airport: IXM — Madurai, ~2–3 h; TRZ — Tiruchirappalli, ~3 h

lake-garda-campione-malcesine.description: Garda is Italy's largest lake, set in a narrow Alpine valley where thermal winds blow like clockwork: the northerly Pelèr in the morning, the southerly Ora in the afternoon. Kiting on the lake is tightly restricted: according to the schools, it's banned in the northern (Trentino) part around Riva and Torbole; you can ride in designated zones — at Campione del Garda and Malcesine (where you usually launch from a school boat). Cool fresh water, mountain scenery, excellent infrastructure.
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.rating_basis: One of Europe's windiest areas, with the Ora and Pelèr thermals for morning and evening sessions (Kitejungle); Riva, Torbole and Campione are known as centres for sailing, windsurfing and kiting (Wikipedia). Kiting is heavily restricted to certain zones — rated lower than for windsurfing
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.waves_note: Fresh water, no waves — short lake chop in a strong Ora
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.hazards: A deep lake with no shallows — you need a rescue service if the wind drops; rocky shores; heavy traffic of yachts, ferries and windsurfers; kiting banned outside permitted zones (fines) — check the current rules locally
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.gustiness_note: The thermal winds blow along the lake on schedule, but near the shores and under the mountains there are holes and gusts; the morning Pelèr is stronger and gustier
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.crowd_note: In summer the lake is packed with windsurfers, yachts and wingfoilers; the kite zones are small
pros: Wind on schedule almost every summer day
Fresh water, no waves and no salt
Easy to reach by car from Central Europe
cons: Strict kiting restrictions: only certain zones and often a boat launch
Deep — if the wind drops it's a long way back to shore (support boat needed)
Cold water outside summer
Lots of windsurfers and yachts
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.wind_dir: S (Ora, afternoon) and N (Pelèr, morning) — along the lake, side-shore
lake-garda-campione-malcesine.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~1 h 40 min; VCE — Venice, ~2 h

lo-stagnone-marsala.description: Lo Stagnone is Sicily's largest lagoon, between Marsala and Trapani — a nature reserve with the islands of Isola Lunga and Mozia and old salt windmills. The water is flat and shallow over a huge area, making it one of Europe's best places for learning, freestyle and foiling. In summer a thermal breeze blows; in spring and autumn, the stronger Mistral and Sirocco.
lo-stagnone-marsala.rating_basis: One of Europe's most popular kite lagoons (Kitejungle): a huge expanse of shallow flat water for learning, freestyle and foiling; kite trips from March to November. Downside — mostly a moderate thermal in summer
lo-stagnone-marsala.waves_note: No waves: knee- to waist-deep flat water across almost the whole lagoon (depth 0.5–2 m)
lo-stagnone-marsala.hazards: Very shallow: injuries from falls, sharp shells/stones — wear booties; nature reserve — keep to the corridors and stay away from the islands and boats; seaweed
lo-stagnone-marsala.gustiness_note: The wind is steady over the open shallow lagoon; in spring and autumn frontal winds reach ~33 kn
lo-stagnone-marsala.crowd_note: In peak season (May–September) lots of students and kiters around the schools, but the lagoon is big
lo-stagnone-marsala.region: Western Sicily, Trapani — the Stagnone lagoon near Marsala
pros: Huge shallow lagoon with perfectly flat water
Warm water in summer, beautiful sunsets and salt windmills
Lots of schools and kite camps, Trapani airport nearby
cons: Summer wind is often moderate (big kites/foil needed)
Crowded around the schools in peak season
Shallow — hitting the bottom when jumping is dangerous; seaweed and mud
lo-stagnone-marsala.wind_dir: Summer: SW–W thermal breeze; spring/autumn: N–NW (Mistral) and SE (Sirocco); side-shore / side-onshore
lo-stagnone-marsala.airport: TPS — Trapani-Birgi, ~10 min; PMO — Palermo, ~1 h 30 min

porto-botte.description: A wide (~2 km) shallow bay in southwest Sardinia with a sandy bottom and a beach about 2 km long. It works best in the northwesterly Mistral, which blows side-onshore here and is boosted by the terrain. Three zones: Il Fortino in the north, the centre, and Is Solinas in the south; Punta Trettu nearby is good for beginners.
porto-botte.rating_basis: Wannakitesurf rates the spot “Great” for all levels; local schools call the bay one of the best places in southwest Sardinia for the Mistral
porto-botte.waves_note: Flat and shallow for ~300 m from shore, then chop in the Mistral; no waves
porto-botte.hazards: Muddy bottom in the northern Il Fortino zone; protected wetlands (birds) — respect the zones; chop in the outer bay in a strong Mistral
porto-botte.gustiness_note: The Mistral is boosted by the Venturi effect and blows steadily; patchy in a light SE
porto-botte.crowd_note: The Is Solinas zone can get busy in summer; the Giba municipality sometimes sets aside a kite corridor
pros: Plenty of room to launch and land
Strong, steady wind in the Mistral
cons: Cold water in winter (~14–15 °C)
Poor in any wind other than NW/W/strong SE
Muddy bottom in the Il Fortino zone
porto-botte.wind_dir: NW (Mistral), side-onshore; also W and strong SE (Sirocco)

porto-pollo-sardinia.description: Porto Pollo is a pair of bays in northern Sardinia near Palau, separated by an isthmus leading to the islet of Isola dei Gabbiani. Wind from the Strait of Bonifacio is boosted by the Venturi effect, so it blows more often here than on the rest of the coast; kiters ride the west side by the river mouth (side-onshore). A classic European summer spot with competitions and a campsite right by the water.
porto-pollo-sardinia.rating_basis: Sardinia's best-known kite spot: the 2016 kite world championship final, rounds of the Italian championship; Robby Naish called it “a perfect natural gym” (it.wikipedia). Kitejungle: season March–October, very crowded in summer
porto-pollo-sardinia.waves_note: On the west side of the isthmus (Porto Liscia, the river mouth) — chop and small waves; the eastern bay, Porto Puddu, is flat but given over to windsurfers in summer
porto-pollo-sardinia.hazards: Boats, swimmers and windsurfers; rocks by the headlands; in an easterly the east side is offshore
porto-pollo-sardinia.gustiness_note: The wind is accelerated by the Venturi effect in the Strait of Bonifacio between Sardinia and Corsica; the Maestrale can be strong and gusty
porto-pollo-sardinia.crowd_note: Very crowded in July–August and on any windy day; in high season the east side is for windsurfers only
porto-pollo-sardinia.region: Northeast Sardinia, Palau — Strait of Bonifacio
pros: Wind more frequent and stronger than at neighbouring beaches (Venturi effect)
Two bays for different wind directions
Warm water in summer, beautiful Gallura scenery
Campsite and schools right at the spot
cons: Very crowded in summer, limited kite zone
The eastern bay is closed to kiting in summer
The Maestrale can be too strong and gusty
porto-pollo-sardinia.wind_dir: W–NW (Maestrale / Ponente) — side-onshore on the west side; E (Levante) — side-offshore on the east side

reschensee-lago-di-resia.description: Reschensee, a reservoir about 6 km long at ~1500 m with the submerged bell tower of Graun, is South Tyrol's main kite spot. In summer (May–October) a reliable southerly valley wind blows; there are shallows for learning and open water for freestyle. In winter the lake freezes over and becomes a playground for snowkiting and ice surfing, hosting snowkite championships.
reschensee-lago-di-resia.rating_basis: One of the best high-altitude kite lakes in the Alps: a reliable summer thermal and, since 2008, German snowkite championships on the ice; downsides — cold water and crowding on the water in peak season
reschensee-lago-di-resia.waves_note: In summer — flat water and light chop, with shallows for beginners; in winter — riding on the frozen, snow-covered lake
reschensee-lago-di-resia.hazards: Ice-cold water; in winter — cracks and changes in the reservoir level under the ice, only go out on confirmed safe ice
reschensee-lago-di-resia.gustiness_note: The valley wind blows along the 6 km lake, steady and reliable in the second half of the day
reschensee-lago-di-resia.crowd_note: Lots of kiters and windsurfers on the lake on windy summer days, quieter in winter
reschensee-lago-di-resia.region: South Tyrol, Reschen Pass (~1500 m), near the Austrian and Swiss borders
pros: Two seasons: summer thermal and snowkiting on the ice
Alpine scenery and the bell tower in the lake
cons: Cold mountain water — a thick wetsuit is a must
Crowded on windy summer days
High altitude: cool even in summer
Ice conditions depend on the winter
reschensee-lago-di-resia.wind_dir: S (summer thermal along the valley), side-shore along the lake; also N in winter
reschensee-lago-di-resia.airport: INN — Innsbruck ~1.5–2 h; BZO — Bolzano ~2 h; MUC / VRN ~3.5–4 h

diani-beach.description: A long white beach south of Mombasa with a reef-protected lagoon. Two monsoon seasons: the warm northerly Kaskazi with flatter water and the strong southerly Kusi with waves on the reef. Soft sand, shallow water and warm water year-round; safaris and snorkelling nearby.
diani-beach.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — 4.3: reliable side-shore wind in two seasons, a wide clear lagoon and a reef with waves, a long-established kite community; Diani was chosen as Kenya's more developed kite destination (Watamu is an alternative with the same rating)
diani-beach.waves_note: Flat water in the lagoon behind the reef (especially in the morning at low tide), chop on the incoming tide; waves on the reef and in the Mlango pass, bigger in the Kusi season
diani-beach.hazards: Shallow reef at big low tides (especially Mlango), chop at high tide, moored boats and swimmers near the sandbanks; sea urchins
diani-beach.gustiness_note: Both monsoons blow steadily along the shore; the Kaskazi is warmer and steadier (~20 knots), the Kusi stronger (25+ knots)
diani-beach.crowd_note: Up to ~30 kites at the main spot by Kenyaways at peak; the Neptune and Baobab sandbanks are almost always empty
diani-beach.region: South coast of Kenya, 35 km south of Mombasa, Indian Ocean
pros: Steady side-shore wind in two seasons
Safaris and snorkelling on windless days
cons: Rainy season April–June
Shallow reef at spring low tides
Pushy beach touts
Flights with connections
diani-beach.airport: MBA — Mombasa, ~1–1.5 h (with the Likoni ferry); UKA — Ukunda, ~10 min

jeju-iho-tewoo.description: Iho Tewoo beach near Jeju airport is the island's main kite spot, with a local school. The wind blows most of the year: strongest in winter (the cold northwest monsoon), while April–May and September–October offer the best mix of wind and warmth. The launch is a narrow beach about 50 m wide between breakwaters.
jeju-iho-tewoo.rating_basis: kitejungle: Jeju is Korea's windiest place (~263 windy days), but the launch is narrow and the spot is for experienced riders; known mainly to local riders
jeju-iho-tewoo.hazards: Breakwaters and concrete walls on either side of the launch, rocky entries on neighbouring beaches, windsurfers, proximity to the airport (about 1 km from the end of the runway)
jeju-iho-tewoo.gustiness_note: 15–30 kn in spring and autumn, 10–20 in summer; the wind is usually a little gusty
jeju-iho-tewoo.crowd_note: Moderate; windsurfers on the water too
cons: Narrow launch (~50 m) between breakwaters
Very cold in winter
Little room to land on either side
jeju-iho-tewoo.wind_dir: NW–N in winter and autumn (monsoon), S in summer

kapchagay-reservoir.description: The Kapchagay Reservoir, 70 km from Almaty, is where Almaty's kiters mostly ride. They ride by pumping stations No. 5–6, where the easterly “Chilik” wind blows steadily, and past the village of Shengeldy (the northern part) there's even more wind. The season runs from late spring to autumn; summer is hot and the water warm.
kapchagay-reservoir.rating_basis: Almaty kiters' main spot: valued for the strong easterly “Chilik” and proximity to the city; downsides — short steep waves, little infrastructure, no dedicated kite stations
kapchagay-reservoir.waves_note: A reservoir ~100 km long: in a strong “Chilik” short steep waves of up to 1–2 m build up
kapchagay-reservoir.hazards: Southerly wind is offshore; short steep waves; far from rescue services
kapchagay-reservoir.gustiness_note: The “Chilik” is steady and strong; the westerly is gusty and unpredictable
kapchagay-reservoir.crowd_note: A local community; a few dozen kites on windy weekends
cons: Steep short waves in strong wind
Hardly any kite schools or rentals
Gusty westerly wind
Heat up to +35 °C and little shade
kapchagay-reservoir.wind_dir: E–SE (“Chilik”) — side-shore; NW (“Balkhash”); W (“Zapad”) — gusty; S — offshore, dangerous

kalpitiya.description: Kalpitiya is a sandy peninsula between the Indian Ocean and Puttalam Lagoon — Sri Lanka's main kite centre, with dozens of kite camps. From mid-May to mid-October a strong southwest monsoon blows; from mid-December to mid-March, a gentler winter wind. The big lagoon is good for learning, and by boat you can reach Vella Island and Dream Spot or do downwinders across Puttalam Lagoon.
kalpitiya.rating_basis: Sri Lanka's main kite resort: two seasons, wind almost daily in summer, more than a dozen spots from flat lagoons to waves (IKSURFMAG, Kitejungle); downsides — fishing nets, jellyfish, basic infrastructure
kalpitiya.waves_note: The big lagoon (~2×1 km) — flat shallow water; Donkey Spot on the ocean side — chop and waves; Vella Island and Dream Spot (summer, by boat) — flat water in the island's lee and open sea on the other side
kalpitiya.hazards: Fishing nets in the lagoons (look out for buoys and flags), jellyfish, muddy bottom in the middle of the lagoon (wear booties), no rescue service on the ocean side at Donkey Spot in summer; some spots require a pass/permit
kalpitiya.gustiness_note: In summer the monsoon is strong and steady, blowing from morning to evening (18–25 kn, peaks up to 30); in winter the wind is lighter (15–20 kn) and picks up by midday
kalpitiya.crowd_note: The big lagoon gets busy around the camps at the height of summer, but dozens of spots around let you escape the crowds; the island spots are empty
kalpitiya.region: North Western Province, Kalpitiya peninsula (Kappalady / Kandakuliya)
pros: Wind almost daily in summer, 18–25 kn
Flat shallow lagoons for learning and freestyle
Lots of spots, island trips and downwinders
cons: Basic infrastructure, life revolves around the camps
Fishing nets in the lagoon
Shoulder months (November, April) — almost no wind
~3–4 h drive from Colombo airport
kalpitiya.wind_dir: SW–W in summer (southwest monsoon, cross-shore); N–NE in winter

mannar-keeri.description: Mannar Island in northern Sri Lanka continues the chain of Adam's Bridge shoals towards India. The summer southwest monsoon strengthens in the strait here, blowing 20–30 kn almost every day, while long shallow beaches and lagoons offer flat water. A wild, uncrowded place for independent riders and kite safaris.
mannar-keeri.rating_basis: Known as Sri Lanka's windiest and emptiest spot — safaris come here from Kalpitiya and head out to the Adam's Bridge shoals (Kitejungle notes a “very remote place”); rated lower for weak infrastructure and few schools
mannar-keeri.waves_note: The shallow coast of the Gulf of Mannar: flat water and chop near shore and in the lagoons (Vankalai, Adam's Bridge shoals); no serious waves
mannar-keeri.hazards: Remoteness and no rescue service, fishing nets and boats, shallows with a shelly bottom, strong wind; the Adam's Bridge shoals are a border zone requiring permits
mannar-keeri.gustiness_note: The summer monsoon strengthens in the strait between India and Sri Lanka — the wind is stronger and steadier than in Kalpitiya; the island has the country's largest wind farm
mannar-keeri.crowd_note: Almost deserted: a few kite camps and safari groups from Kalpitiya
mannar-keeri.region: Northern Province, Mannar Island (Gulf of Mannar)
pros: Very steady, strong wind from June to September
Safaris to the Adam's Bridge shoals
cons: Remote: 5–6 h from Colombo
Few schools and rentals, basic accommodation
Strong wind — not for beginners
Light, irregular wind in winter
mannar-keeri.wind_dir: SW–W (southwest monsoon), side-onshore; N–NE in winter
mannar-keeri.airport: CMB — Colombo, ~5–6 h by car; JAF — Jaffna, ~2 h

dakhla-lagoon.description: A huge shallow lagoon on the Dakhla peninsula in the middle of the Sahara — one of the windiest and best-known kite places in the world. The camps sit at the northern tip of the lagoon (PK25), from where you can ride flat water, go on downwinders to the White Dune and Dragon Island, and drive out to the waves at Oum El Bouir.
dakhla-lagoon.rating_basis: Features on almost every world top list: a 45 km lagoon, ~340 windy days a year (IKSURFMAG), flat water for freestyle and wave spots nearby; downsides — remoteness and cold nights
dakhla-lagoon.waves_note: In the lagoon it's flat at low tide and choppy at high tide, no waves; Speed Spot is glassy at low water; waves at the Oum El Bouir right-hand point break (bigger in winter)
dakhla-lagoon.hazards: Currents and strong wind in the lagoon, tides change the depth; rocks and shorebreak at the wave spots
dakhla-lagoon.gustiness_note: The trade wind blows steadily, lighter in the morning and building by 14:00; up to 30–35 knots in summer
dakhla-lagoon.crowd_note: Up to 7 camps at the northern tip of the lagoon — busy by the camps, but the lagoon is huge; Speed Spot gets packed at low water
pros: Huge lagoon with flat, shallow water
Camp format — step out of your bungalow and onto the water
cons: Remote: flights via Casablanca
Cold nights and 18–22 °C water — wetsuit needed
Unreliable internet
A 4×4 is needed for the distant spots
dakhla-lagoon.airport: VIL — Dakhla, ~30–40 min to the camps

essaouira.description: An atmospheric fortified town with a UNESCO-listed medina and a wide sandy bay where the northeasterly trade wind blows almost all year. The main beach has chop and small waves, there's a flat lagoon at the river mouth nearby, and 20 km away are the wave spots of Sidi Kaouki and Moulay. Everything is within walking distance, and accommodation and food are cheap.
essaouira.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: the “Wind City”, with trade winds almost year-round, a big bay, direct flights from Europe and a low cost of living; downsides — cold water, sandblasting and gusty wind
essaouira.waves_note: Chop and small waves on the main beach (bigger at the left end of the bay), no shorebreak; the lagoon at the river mouth is flat but cramped
essaouira.hazards: Strong wind of up to 40 knots in summer, waves at the left end of the bay, shifting depths in the lagoon, strong sun
essaouira.gustiness_note: In summer the trade wind is steady and can reach 35–40 knots; blowing sand from the beach and cold wind
essaouira.crowd_note: The main bay is very big — plenty of room; the small lagoon fills up with just ~6 kites
pros: Wind almost year-round, very steady in summer
cons: Cold water, 17–21 °C — a 3–4 mm wetsuit is needed
Sandblasting and chilly wind on the beach
The wind can be too strong in summer
Little alcohol or nightlife
essaouira.airport: ESU — Essaouira, ~20 min; RAK — Marrakesh, ~2.5–3 h

moulay-bousselham.description: A fishing village on Morocco's northern Atlantic coast with a long sandy beach and a beach break popular with surfers from Casablanca and Rabat. Kiting is possible in summer in the northerly trade wind. The Merja Zerga lagoon south of the village is a bird reserve, not a kite zone.
moulay-bousselham.rating_basis: A little-known spot: the kite-and-windsurfing-guide describes it as a long sandy beach with a beach break where kiting is possible when the trade wind is strong enough; there are hardly any dedicated schools or kiter reviews
moulay-bousselham.waves_note: Atlantic beach break; big waves in winter, smaller in summer
moulay-bousselham.hazards: Beach break and currents at the lagoon mouth; the lagoon is a reserve (no kiting); offshore in an easterly
moulay-bousselham.gustiness_note: Kiting is only possible when the trade wind is strong enough; the winter easterly is offshore
moulay-bousselham.crowd_note: Only a handful of kiters; lots of holidaymakers and surfers on the beach in summer
pros: Empty water and a long beach
Not far from Rabat and Tangier
cons: No kite schools or rentals
Unsteady wind, offshore in winter
Little information about the spot
moulay-bousselham.wind_dir: N–NE in summer (trade wind), side-onshore; in winter often E — offshore
moulay-bousselham.airport: RBA — Rabat-Salé, ~1.5–2 h; TNG — Tangier, ~2 h

ulcinj-velika-plaza.description: Velika Plaža is a 13 km sandy beach southeast of Ulcinj, stretching to the Albanian border and Ada Bojana island. In summer a steady 12–25 kn thermal blows almost every day from midday to sunset; the water is shallow and warm (25+ °C), with no shorebreak. A popular ~7 km downwinder leads to the Bojana river delta, with flat water between the sandbars.
ulcinj-velika-plaza.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — rating 4.0, “one of the last ‘hidden’ kite spots in Europe”: a wide sandy beach, waist-deep water, no shorebreak and no sharp obstacles
ulcinj-velika-plaza.waves_note: Usually chop; small waves only after bad weather. At the end of the ~7 km downwinder — flat water between sandbars in the Bojana delta
ulcinj-velika-plaza.hazards: No sharp obstacles; at the Bojana mouth — current and shifting sandbanks, so the downwinder is best done as an organised trip
ulcinj-velika-plaza.gustiness_note: A “super-steady” thermal almost daily from midday to sunset; according to locals, Windguru underestimates the real wind
ulcinj-velika-plaza.crowd_note: The kite zone is usually quiet; with a 13 km beach there's plenty of room
pros: Waist-deep shallow water and a wide sandy beach — easy for beginners
Downwinder to flat water in the Bojana delta
cons: Little wind outside May–September
Far from airports (Podgorica ~1 h 15 min, Tivat ~1.5–2 h)
Few online forecasts predict the wind accurately
ulcinj-velika-plaza.airport: TGD — Podgorica, ~1 h 15 min; TIV — Tivat, ~1.5–2 h

sakalava-bay.description: A picturesque bay in northern Madagascar near the town of Diego Suarez: a sand spit with flat water inside the reef and waves outside. From April to November the strong southeasterly “Varatraza” trade wind blows almost daily. The Emerald Sea (Babaomby) nearby is great for downwinders and safari trips.
sakalava-bay.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — 4.3: “the most beautiful bay in the Diego Suarez area”, combining strong steady wind, flat water, waves and reef protection; neighbouring Babaomby is among the ten windiest places on the planet according to Windguru
sakalava-bay.waves_note: Glassy flat water at the sand spit, with the bay sheltered by the reef; waves further out on the reef, no shorebreak
sakalava-bay.hazards: Strong wind, reef and waves outside the bay, gusts near the mangroves; malaria region
sakalava-bay.gustiness_note: The trade wind is very steady — in 2017 only 7 of the season's 245 days had wind under 15 knots; gusty near the fishing village because of the mangroves
sakalava-bay.crowd_note: A few lodges with kite stations on a big bay — plenty of room
sakalava-bay.region: Northern tip of Madagascar, Antsiranana (Diego Suarez), Indian Ocean
pros: One of the steadiest and strongest winds in the world (April–November)
Flat water and waves in the same bay
Inexpensive accommodation (€40–80 for a double room)
cons: Complicated logistics: flights via Antananarivo / Paris
Little infrastructure, internet mostly for lodge guests
Summer (Dec–Mar) is the rainy season with no wind

le-morne.description: A peninsula beneath Le Morne Brabant mountain (UNESCO) in southwest Mauritius: a huge shallow flat-water lagoon for learning and freestyle and a barrier reef with waves for every level — from the gentle Manawa to the legendary One Eye. The best wind and swell come in the southern winter (June–November). Hotels sit right on the water.
le-morne.rating_basis: Famous for One Eye — one of the world's best kite waves; IKSURFMAG notes conditions for all levels (lagoon, easy and expert waves within ~1.5 km), ~60% of days > 4 Bft from June to November, but the wind is fickle
le-morne.waves_note: A huge shallow flat-water lagoon; occasional shorebreak at Main Beach; on the reef — Manawa (a gentle left), Chameaux and the legendary One Eye (barrels up to triple overhead, experts only)
le-morne.hazards: Coral in the lagoon, shallow reef and powerful waves at One Eye and Chameaux, currents in the reef passes, shorebreak at Main Beach in a swell
le-morne.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady in direction, but the wind is “fickle” — guides recommend a 2-week trip; Le Morne mountain casts a wind shadow in places
le-morne.crowd_note: Main Beach and the lagoon are busy in peak season; on small days One Eye has lots of beginners on the wave
pros: Lagoon and world-class waves close together
Hotels right on the water, beautiful scenery
cons: Fickle wind — risk of getting skunked
Expensive resort hotels
Coral on the lagoon floor — booties needed
Quiet nightlife
le-morne.wind_dir: SE–ESE (trade wind), cross-shore / onshore from the left; cross-offshore at the Manawa wave

isla-blanca-cancun.description: A narrow sand spit north of Cancún: the Caribbean on one side, a shallow flat lagoon on the other. The season runs from November to June: northerly “nortes” in winter, easterly wind in spring. The main points are the Ikarus camp and La Punta at the tip of the spit, which works in almost any wind direction.
isla-blanca-cancun.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG calls La Punta one of the easiest places in the world to learn; Ikarus is the region's main spot in a northerly
isla-blanca-cancun.waves_note: The lagoon is flat and shallow; in a northerly over 25 kn chop builds at Ikarus
isla-blanca-cancun.hazards: Cars can get stuck in the sand — stick to the beaten tracks; chop in a strong northerly; offshore at the Hotel Zone beaches
isla-blanca-cancun.gustiness_note: The nortes (November–April) are strong and cool; from April the wind veers to E–SE and settles
isla-blanca-cancun.crowd_note: In a northerly, riders from all along the coast flock to Ikarus
pros: Shallow flat lagoon — ideal for learning and freestyle
cons: Little public transport (4 minibuses a day)
Almost no internet
Little wind in summer and autumn, hurricane season
isla-blanca-cancun.wind_dir: N–NE in winter (nortes), E–SE in spring; side/side-off in the lagoon

la-ventana.description: A dusty fishing village on the Sea of Cortez that turns into the kite capital of Baja California in winter. From November to March the northerly “El Norte” blows, boosted by thermals — an almost daily steady wind along the long beach opposite Cerralvo Island. The water is choppy and gets deep right off the beach, so beginners are better off with an instructor and a boat; El Sargento and Los Barriles are nearby.
la-ventana.rating_basis: North America's main winter kite spot, on the Sea of Cortez; Kitejungle notes a high season of November–March and conditions for all levels; the community rates the “El Norte” as reliable and the campsite atmosphere as relaxed
la-ventana.waves_note: No waves — chop and wind swell; deep almost right off the beach
la-ventana.hazards: Rocks on parts of the beach, stingrays in the shallows (shuffle your feet), strong “El Norte” during fronts
la-ventana.gustiness_note: The winter northerly “El Norte”, boosted by daytime thermals in the bay between Cerralvo Island and the mountains; usually steady
la-ventana.crowd_note: Lots of kiters from the US and Canada at the height of the winter season, but with a long beach and deep water there's plenty of room
la-ventana.region: Baja California Sur, Sea of Cortez coast (≈45 km from La Paz)
pros: Lots of room on the water
Close to La Paz and Los Cabos
cons: Water ~20 °C in winter — a 3/2 wetsuit is needed
Deep near shore — harder for beginners
Practically no wind in summer
la-ventana.airport: SJD — San José del Cabo, ~2 h; LAP — La Paz, ~1 h

brouwersdam.description: The Brouwersdam is a 6.5 km dam in the Rhine–Meuse delta between the islands of Goeree-Overflakkee and Schouwen-Duiveland. On one side is a North Sea beach with chop and waves, on the other the saltwater Lake Grevelingen with flat water, so you can ride in almost any wind. The wind is frontal and stronger in autumn and winter; wetsuit in summer, drysuit in winter.
brouwersdam.rating_basis: The Netherlands' best-known kite spot: a 6.5 km dam with beaches on both the sea and the lake — you can ride in almost any wind direction; popular with kiters and windsurfers (en.wikipedia)
brouwersdam.waves_note: On the North Sea side — chop and small waves in westerly winds; on the Lake Grevelingen side — flat water in easterly winds
brouwersdam.hazards: Cold water and hypothermia; breakwaters and the dam's stone slopes; currents at the Brouwerssluis sluice; swimming zones in summer — keep to the kite zones
brouwersdam.gustiness_note: The sea wind over the North Sea is steady; storm fronts are frequent in autumn and winter
brouwersdam.crowd_note: Huge numbers of kiters from the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany on windy weekends; beaches full of holidaymakers in summer
brouwersdam.region: Zeeland / South Holland — the dam between Goeree-Overflakkee and Schouwen-Duiveland
pros: Two sides of the dam — a spot for almost any wind direction
Long sandy beaches, lots of room
Easy to reach by car (Rotterdam ~45 min)
cons: Cold water (5–20 °C), drysuit needed in winter
Changeable weather, lighter wind in summer
Crowded on windy weekends
brouwersdam.wind_dir: SW–W–NW — side-shore / side-onshore on the sea side; E–NE — on Lake Grevelingen
brouwersdam.airport: RTM — Rotterdam, ~45 min; AMS — Amsterdam, ~1 h 30 min; EIN — Eindhoven, ~1 h 30 min

haugastol-hardangervidda.description: Haugastøl is a base village on the edge of the Hardangervidda plateau on the Oslo–Bergen railway — a world mecca of snowkiting and home of the Red Bull Ragnarok race. All around are dozens of frozen lakes and hills for every level: from a flat lake 25 m from the hotel to long expeditions across the plateau. High season is February–May; the best powder is from January to early March.
haugastol-hardangervidda.rating_basis: Considered one of the best snowkiting places in the world: >3400 km² of rideable plateau, steady wind, the legendary Red Bull Ragnarok race; downsides — harsh weather and road closures in storms
haugastol-hardangervidda.waves_note: Frozen lakes (Sløtfjorden by the hotel, Lillevann, Nygårdsvann, Skiftesjøen) and a hilly plateau — from flat “training” fields to terrain and kickers
haugastol-hardangervidda.hazards: Cracks and overflow water on the ice, rocks, open water near dams and rivers, whiteout and frostbite; long solo trips only with navigation
haugastol-hardangervidda.gustiness_note: The wind is steady on the open plateau; near the mountains (Halne, Sløtfjorden) some directions are gusty; in an easterly the wind is stronger in the west of the plateau
haugastol-hardangervidda.crowd_note: Busy by the hotel during Ragnarok and at Easter, but the plateau is huge — the distant spots are almost empty
haugastol-hardangervidda.region: Vestland / Viken, between Oslo and Bergen, ~1000 m
pros: Huge open plateau and dozens of spots
Steady wind from almost any direction
Season lasts until May, long spring days
cons: Very cold and windy, rapidly changing weather
Norway is expensive
The road across the plateau closes in storms
Early season (Oct–Jan) — little snow and short daylight
haugastol-hardangervidda.wind_dir: W and E (along the plateau); all directions work at most spots
haugastol-hardangervidda.airport: OSL — Oslo Gardermoen ~4 h / BGO — Bergen ~4 h; Bergensbanen train to Haugastøl station

auckland-orewa.description: Orewa is a long sandy beach in north Auckland, one of the city's main spots in northerly and easterly winds. With so many bays, Auckland has a spot for almost any direction: Orewa, St Heliers and The Spit with flat water, Shakespeare Regional Park, and ocean-facing Muriwai with waves. The wind is frontal; the best period is spring (September–November).
auckland-orewa.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: you can ride in Auckland year-round, the windiest months being June–November; Orewa suits both beginners and experienced riders. It's a local “home” spot rather than a world-class kite resort
auckland-orewa.waves_note: A 4 km beach on the Hauraki Gulf: in N–NE and E — wind waves with no shorebreak; smoother at low tide. Nearby in Auckland there are flat-water spots (St Heliers, The Spit, Shoal Bay) and the Muriwai surf beach
auckland-orewa.hazards: Tides (low tide is better), swimmers in summer, gusts as fronts pass through, cold water in winter; at nearby Muriwai — powerful waves and currents
auckland-orewa.gustiness_note: The wind is mainly frontal and changes with the weather; around New Year there can be strong easterlies, and in summer a sea breeze adds to it
auckland-orewa.crowd_note: A long beach; on windy weekends kiters come from all over Auckland
auckland-orewa.region: Auckland, Hibiscus Coast (Hauraki Gulf), ~35 km north of the centre
pros: Long beach with no shorebreak, shallow at low tide
Many spots for different directions in one city
Easy to combine with a trip around New Zealand
cons: Frontal, irregular wind
Cool water: 14 °C in winter, a 4/3 wetsuit is needed
A long and expensive flight
Tide-dependent

wellington-plimmerton.description: Onehunga Bay in Whitireia Park, opposite Plimmerton, is the main NW spot around Wellington: flat water inside the bay, waves on the bank outside. It's usually windier here than on the rest of the Kāpiti Coast, but gentler than in Wellington itself. Lyall Bay in the city, by the airport, is a wave spot for experts only.
wellington-plimmerton.rating_basis: kitejungle: “waves outside, flat water inside — simply fantastic in a NW”; the spot is popular with kiters and windsurfers. Lyall Bay in the city is for the very experienced only
wellington-plimmerton.waves_note: Flat inside, waves on the sandbank outside (highly tide-dependent); the best waves come in a gusty N
wellington-plimmerton.hazards: Gusty wind in a N, dangerous NE; rocks and pebbles at the launch; the waves on the bank depend on the tide
wellington-plimmerton.gustiness_note: Strong gusts in N and NE; steadier in NW and W
wellington-plimmerton.crowd_note: Popular with windsurfers, can get crowded
pros: Flat water and waves in one place
cons: Strong gusts in N/NE
Cold water (12–17 °C)
Rocky, pebbly launch; the park closes before sunset
wellington-plimmerton.wind_dir: NW (best), works W–N; N and NE gusty, NE dangerous

masirah-island.description: A desert island off the coast of Oman where the strong southwest monsoon (khareef) arrives in summer. The west coast has shallow flat bays for freeriding and learning; the east coast has ocean waves for advanced riders. Logistics usually go through tour operators: a 5-hour drive from Muscat plus a ferry; often combined with the Barr Al Hikman lagoons.
masirah-island.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — 4.8 for a kite trip around Oman (Barr Al Hikman + Masirah): 20–35 knots all summer, flat bays in the west and waves up to 5 m in the east, almost empty water; downsides — no rescue boats and complicated logistics
masirah-island.waves_note: West coast — flat bays ~1.7 m deep at high tide, no shorebreak; east coast — 2–3 m waves (up to ~5 m), a right-hander, shorebreak
masirah-island.hazards: No rescue on the water, rocks on the way out at Khaseet, powerful waves in the east; heat and sun
masirah-island.gustiness_note: The summer monsoon blows very steadily and strongly — from mid-June to the end of August with hardly a break
masirah-island.crowd_note: A wild island — only a handful of people on the water; sometimes windsurfers at the eastern spots
masirah-island.region: Arabian Sea, Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate
pros: Powerful, steady summer wind when other places are calm
Flat water and big waves on the same island
cons: Short season — mid-June to August
Remote: 5 h from Muscat + ferry
No rescue boats, little infrastructure
Very hot on shore in summer
masirah-island.wind_dir: S–SW (southwest monsoon), side-onshore in the west, side-offshore in the east
masirah-island.airport: MCT — Muscat, ~5 h by car + ferry

punta-chame.description: A narrow sandy peninsula on Panama's Pacific coast where in the dry season (December–April) the northerly trade wind blows across the isthmus. Big tides change the spot through the day: at low tide it's shallow for beginners, at high tide there are ramps for jumping, and downwind there are flat-water lagoons for freestyle. Infrastructure is modest — a few guesthouses and kite centres.
punta-chame.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: Panama's main kite spot — dry season December–April, a huge beach, flat-water lagoons and a sandbank; the spot is rarely crowded
punta-chame.waves_note: Small waves with no shorebreak on the main beach, flatter in the morning and at low tide; downwind — a mini lagoon (5–10 min) and a big lagoon (20 min) with flat water at mid tide; a sandbank 20 min upwind — only at spring low tide
punta-chame.hazards: Stingrays on the main beach (shuffle your feet), obstacles downwind of the big lagoon, the remote sandbank — only with a buddy; strong tidal currents
punta-chame.gustiness_note: The dry-season trade wind from the north across the isthmus; around midday the wind can drop, and there are windless days
punta-chame.crowd_note: The main beach is huge and rarely crowded, almost empty in the morning; the mini lagoon is busier in the evening
punta-chame.region: Western Panama, Pacific coast (≈1.5–2 h from Panama City)
pros: Suits all levels (depending on the tide)
cons: Season only December–April
Highly tide-dependent
The wind can dip during the day, very hot

paracas.description: The desert bay of Paracas, 3–4 h south of Lima, is Peru's main kite spot. The southerly thermal wind kicks in around midday and can be very strong by three in the afternoon. Near the beach there's chop and plenty of room for beginners; on the upwind side and at the far spot the water is glassy; an hour's drive away is Laguna Grande in the reserve.
paracas.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: steady wind ~300 days a year, suits all levels; kitejungle — best season November–April
paracas.waves_note: Chop near the beach, perfectly flat water on the upwind side of the bay; no waves
paracas.hazards: A cross-offshore component to the wind, very strong gusts in the afternoon, cool water
paracas.gustiness_note: Almost calm in the morning; the wind builds by midday and peaks around 15:00 (sometimes 30–40 kn); it can be gusty in the middle of the day
paracas.crowd_note: Lots of beginners near shore, but the bay is big — finding room is easy
paracas.region: Ica, Paracas Bay (next to the national reserve)
pros: Suits all levels, schools right on the beach
cons: Cool water, 16–22 °C
No wind in the morning
Fine sand gets into your gear
Far from Lima
paracas.wind_dir: S–SSW, cross / cross-off from the left

boracay-bulabog.description: Bulabog is Boracay's east beach: a reef-sheltered lagoon reserved exclusively for kiting and windsurfing. From late October to April the northeast Amihan monsoon blows; more than a dozen schools line the beach, and the famous White Beach with its restaurants and bars is a 5-minute walk away.
boracay-bulabog.rating_basis: The Philippines' main kite hub (Kitejungle); IKSURFMAG describes a reliable 15–25 kn Amihan and a flat lagoon behind the reef with no shorebreak; downside — crowding in peak season
boracay-bulabog.waves_note: A flat-water lagoon inside the reef, with chop in strong wind; waves on the outer reef. No shorebreak; the water is smoother in the morning and at certain stages of the tide
boracay-bulabog.hazards: Coral reef and shallows at low tide, crowding in the lagoon, waves on the outer reef; chop in strong wind
boracay-bulabog.gustiness_note: The northeast Amihan monsoon blows almost constantly from late October to April, averaging 18–20 kn; often stronger in the morning
boracay-bulabog.crowd_note: Very crowded in the narrow lagoon in peak season — dozens of kites and students at once
boracay-bulabog.region: Aklan Province, Boracay Island, east coast
pros: Flat water behind the reef, no shorebreak
Excellent resort infrastructure and nightlife nearby
cons: Very crowded in peak season
Reef and shallows at low tide
Nowhere to ride out of season (May–September)
Expensive by Philippine standards
boracay-bulabog.airport: MPH — Caticlan, ~30 min + 15 min ferry; KLO — Kalibo, ~1.5 h

cuyo-capusan.description: Cuyo is a small island (13×7 km) in the Sulu Sea between Palawan and Panay, known for its strong, reliable northeast monsoon from November to April. The main spot is Capusan beach with its sand spit: a shallow lagoon for learning on one side, flat water for freestyle on the other. The second spot is Victoria's Beach by the Anino's Retreat kite resort.
cuyo-capusan.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG describes Cuyo as an island with a strong, steady Amihan (20–35 kn, calm days are rare) and two types of water by the sand spit — from learning to freestyle; downside — complicated logistics
cuyo-capusan.waves_note: A sand spit separates the spot from the sea: on the right, shallow knee- to waist-deep water with light chop; on the left, perfectly flat water for freestyle; no waves or shorebreak
cuyo-capusan.hazards: Coral and seagrass in the shallows to the right of the spit, gusty offshore wind on the left (it can carry you towards the boats), tide-dependent, far from medical care
cuyo-capusan.gustiness_note: The Amihan is often 20–35 kn (7–9 m kites); to the right of the spit the wind is steady, on the left it's offshore and gusty
cuyo-capusan.crowd_note: A quiet, remote island with only a handful of riders on the water
pros: Flat water and shallows by the spit
cons: Hard to reach: ferry from Puerto Princesa ~4 times a week or small planes with a 20 kg baggage limit
Weak internet, little infrastructure
Offshore to the left of the spit — a confident level is needed
No established schools or rentals
cuyo-capusan.wind_dir: NE (Amihan): cross-onshore on the right, offshore on the left
cuyo-capusan.airport: CYU — Cuyo (Air Juan flights); PPS — Puerto Princesa + ferry

lagoa-de-obidos.description: Óbidos Lagoon is a large shallow lagoon on the Atlantic coast an hour north of Lisbon, connected to the ocean at Foz do Arelho. In summer the thermal Nortada blows almost every afternoon, and the water is flat and waist-deep over a large area — ideal for learning, freestyle and foiling. There's an ocean beach nearby for wave riding.
lagoa-de-obidos.rating_basis: Portugal's largest coastal lagoon (~6.9 km², average depth ~2 m) — one of Europe's best places for learning and flat-water freestyle; Kitejungle: suits all levels, medium crowds
lagoa-de-obidos.waves_note: No waves in the lagoon — flat water and light chop; waves nearby on the Foz do Arelho ocean beach
lagoa-de-obidos.hazards: Strong tidal currents at the lagoon mouth (don't drift into the channel to the ocean); sandbanks and mud at low tide; boats and fishermen
lagoa-de-obidos.gustiness_note: The summer thermal Nortada builds by midday and blows fairly steadily over the open lagoon
lagoa-de-obidos.crowd_note: Lots of schools and students in the shallows in summer, but there's plenty of room on the lagoon
lagoa-de-obidos.region: Central Portugal, Silver Coast (Foz do Arelho / Óbidos)
pros: Flat shallow water over a large area
Steady thermal wind on summer afternoons
An hour from Lisbon, with Peniche and Óbidos nearby
cons: Unreliable wind outside summer
Tides change the depth, strong currents at the mouth
Muddy bottom in places
Cool water outside summer

praia-do-guincho.description: Guincho is a wide sandy beach on the Atlantic coast 30 minutes from Lisbon, at the foot of the Sintra hills. In summer a strong northerly Nortada blows almost every sunny day, and there are ocean waves year-round; it's a spot for confident riders — freeride, waves, big air. The water is cold even in summer because of upwelling.
praia-do-guincho.rating_basis: A legendary spot near Lisbon that has hosted kite and windsurf world championship events; in summer it's “always windy on a sunny day”, up to 40 kn (Kitejungle). Challenging conditions: waves, currents, cold water — not for beginners
praia-do-guincho.waves_note: Atlantic beach break: from chop and small waves in summer to big waves in winter; at low and mid tide the waves break further out, at full high tide there's a very powerful shorebreak
praia-do-guincho.hazards: Strong currents and rips; powerful shorebreak at high tide; rocks on the beach and in the water at the edges; gusty wind near the cliffs; cold water
praia-do-guincho.gustiness_note: The Nortada, boosted by the Sintra hills, reaches 30–40 kn in summer; the wind off the cliffs at the north end of the beach is gusty
praia-do-guincho.crowd_note: Lots of surfers and Lisbon day-trippers on summer weekends; few kiters on the water because the spot is demanding
pros: 30 minutes from Lisbon, easy to combine with the city
cons: Cold water (15–20 °C) — a 4/3 wetsuit year-round
Powerful surf and currents, not for beginners
Gusts near the cliffs, the wind can be too strong

viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.description: Cabedelo is a wide sandy beach on the south bank of the Lima river mouth, opposite the town of Viana do Castelo in northern Portugal. In summer a 15–25 kn thermal Nortada blows every afternoon; the estuary is shallow and flat — easy for learning — while neighbouring Rodanho has waves. Several schools (Kite Voodoo, Modo Experto and others), a kite shop and rentals.
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.rating_basis: Considered one of Portugal's best kite spots (pt.wikipedia); TheKiteSpot — reliable wind from April to October, conditions for all levels. Downside — cold water
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.waves_note: At Cabedelo and in the estuary — flat water to chop; on neighbouring Rodanho beach — waves of 2 m+ on the sandbanks
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.hazards: Currents at the mouth of the Lima, especially at low tide; tides change the depth; in offshore wind — only with the school's safety boat
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.gustiness_note: The Nortada gets a thermal boost (up to +50% over the forecast), peaking around 16:00; you need a bigger kite in the morning
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.crowd_note: Beaches are busy in summer (June–August), but there's plenty of room on the water
pros: Waist-deep shallows in the Cabedelo zone — easy for beginners
cons: Cold water (14–20 °C), a 4/3 wetsuit almost always
Little wind in the morning — riding is in the afternoon
Unreliable wind out of season
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.wind_dir: N–NW (Nortada), side-shore / side-onshore; SW in winter (Suestada)
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo.airport: OPO — Porto, ~50 min (~76 km); VGO — Vigo, ~1 h (~99 km)

baikal-maloe-more.description: The Maloye More (“Small Sea”) is the strait between Baikal's western shore and Olkhon Island, with shallow, warm bays (Kurkut, Mukhor) where you can ride flat water in summer. In winter the wind blows the snow away and the ice of the Maloye More becomes a vast playground for ice- and snowkiting (best in February–March, when the ice is over 70 cm thick). A place for experienced riders: the wind is strong and very gusty.
baikal-maloe-more.rating_basis: Exotic: riding on Baikal's clear ice in February–March and summer sessions on the warm shallow bays of the Maloye More; downsides — harsh climate, the gusty Sarma and remoteness
baikal-maloe-more.waves_note: In summer the shallow Kurkut Bay is flat, while the open Maloye More gets steep waves in strong wind; in winter — smooth clear ice, swept of snow by the Sarma
baikal-maloe-more.hazards: The Sarma (gusts up to 40 m/s), cracks and pressure ridges on the ice, open-water holes, frostbite; the water in open Baikal is very cold even in summer
baikal-maloe-more.gustiness_note: The Sarma is a stormy katabatic wind from the Sarma river valley, with gusts up to 40 m/s; in summer the wind is unsteady
baikal-maloe-more.crowd_note: Only a handful of kiters, mostly visiting groups and expeditions
pros: Unique riding on Baikal's clear ice
cons: The Sarma — very strong, gusty wind
Frosts down to −25…−30 °C with wind in winter
Cold water in open Baikal
Remote: ~5–6 h from Irkutsk, dirt roads
baikal-maloe-more.wind_dir: NW (Sarma, the “Gornaya”), also NE–E along the Maloye More; side/side-off
baikal-maloe-more.airport: IKT — Irkutsk, ~5–6 h by car (~250 km)

blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.description: The Bugaz Spit, 100–300 m wide, between the Black Sea and the shallow Bugaz lagoon (liman) near the village of Blagoveshchenskaya, is southern Russia's main kite resort. Most riding is on the flat, shallow lagoon, which is easy to learn on; on the sea side there's chop and small waves in westerly winds. The season runs from May to October, the best months being June–September.
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.rating_basis: Russia's best-known kite spot (IKSURFMAG: 3.5/5); valued for its shallow flat lagoon and well-developed school infrastructure; downsides — moderate and not always steady wind
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.waves_note: Lagoon side of the spit — flat shallow water; sea side in westerly/southwesterly winds — chop and small waves
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.hazards: Strong sun, shallows with a shell-rock bottom; protected area — restrictions on parking and structures
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.gustiness_note: The wind is mostly moderate, building during the day and dying down by sunset; having crossed the spit, it can be gusty near the lagoon shore
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.crowd_note: About a dozen kite stations operate on the spit in summer; lots of students on the lagoon
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.region: Krasnodar Krai, Bugaz Spit, Black Sea / Bugaz lagoon
pros: Shallow flat lagoon — ideal for learning
Lots of Russian-speaking schools and kite camps
A kite park with sliders is set up in season
cons: Moderate wind, big kites needed; windless weeks happen
A wild spit: no shade, little infrastructure
Paid access to the spit, sandy road
Seaweed in the lagoon
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.wind_dir: SW–W (across the spit, side-off on the lagoon); in N–NE people ride at nearby flat-water sections
blagoveshchenskaya-anapa.airport: AAQ — Anapa, ~35 min (airport operations restricted since 2022 — check the status); Anapa railway station ~30 min

dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.description: Dolgaya Spit is an 18 km sandy spit near the village of Dolzhanskaya, separating the open Sea of Azov from the shallow Taganrog Bay. In almost any wind direction one side of the spit is flat and the other has waves, so beginners and freestylers alike love it. The season runs from May to September–October; every September the “Dolzhanka DA!” festival takes place.
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.rating_basis: A cult spot for windsurfers and kiters in southern Russia (the “Dolzhanka DA!” festival); valued for the choice between the flat and wavy sides of the spit; downsides — murky water and weak infrastructure
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.waves_note: The spit separates the Sea of Azov from Taganrog Bay: in a given wind one side is flat, the other has short wind waves of up to 1 m
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.hazards: Strong currents and whirlpools at the tip of the spit; offshore on one of the sides — let the rescuers know; fishing nets
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.gustiness_note: The wind comes off open water and is steady; on the “leeward” side of the spit it's slightly patchy near shore
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.crowd_note: Busy on the spit on summer weekends, but plenty of room on the water
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.region: Krasnodar Krai, Sea of Azov / Taganrog Bay
pros: Flat and wavy water a hundred metres apart
Wind off open water, no obstacles
cons: Murky water, seaweed in places
Far from airports
Little comfortable accommodation right on the spit
A thick wetsuit is needed in May and September
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.wind_dir: E–NE (Nizovka) and W–SW (Verkhovka); there's always a side of the spit with side-shore wind
dolzhanskaya-dolgaya-spit.airport: ROV — Rostov-on-Don (Platov), ~3 h (closed under restrictions since 2022 — check); train to Yeysk (~40 km)

pleshcheyevo-lake.description: A large lake (about 51 km²) in a national park near Pereslavl-Zalessky — the main kite spot within easy reach of Moscow. In summer people ride flat water with wide, gently sloping shallows near shore; in winter, on the ice and snow — snowkite camps and races are held here. The wind is frontal, so you have to come when the forecast is right.
pleshcheyevo-lake.rating_basis: Muscovites' most popular “weekend” spot in summer and winter; valued for its proximity to Moscow, the shallows near shore and snowkiting on the ice; downside — unsteady wind
pleshcheyevo-lake.waves_note: Flat water in summer, light chop in strong wind; in winter — riding on the ice and snow of the lake (when going out on the ice is permitted)
pleshcheyevo-lake.hazards: Thin ice at the start and end of winter, open holes near river mouths and springs (especially in March); gusty wind off the land
pleshcheyevo-lake.gustiness_note: Wind from the land crosses forests and hills — gusty near shore, steadier in the middle of the lake; in summer it builds during the day
pleshcheyevo-lake.crowd_note: Lots of kiters from Moscow on windy weekends, quiet on weekdays
pros: Shallows near shore — easy to learn
Two seasons: water in summer and snowkiting on the ice in winter
cons: Unsteady wind — many windless days in summer
Gusty near shore
Going out on the ice only with official permission
National park — restrictions on access and parking
pleshcheyevo-lake.wind_dir: W–SW and N–NW (frontal); pick the shore to suit the direction
pleshcheyevo-lake.airport: SVO / DME — Moscow, ~2.5–3 h by car

sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.description: The “Dyuny” (Dunes) beach in Sestroretsk on the north shore of the Gulf of Finland is the most popular kite spot within St Petersburg. The shallows are good for learning, and westerly winds bring a short wave. The season runs from June to October, with riding only when frontal wind is forecast; the water warms to ~19 °C only in July–August.
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.rating_basis: St Petersburg's main kite spot (wannakitesurf: 3/5, “for all levels”); easy to get to from the city, but the wind is irregular, the water cool and the beaches crowded in summer
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.waves_note: A shallow gulf: in westerly winds — short wind waves and chop; in easterlies — flat near shore
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.hazards: Offshore in E–NE wind, cold water (hypothermia in spring and autumn), swimmers on the beach
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.gustiness_note: Frontal wind, steadier off the sea; gusty from the east because of forest and buildings
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.crowd_note: Lots of holidaymakers on the beaches in summer — launch away from swimmers
sestroretsk-gulf-of-finland.region: St Petersburg, Kurortny District, Gulf of Finland
pros: Within St Petersburg, 40 min from the centre
cons: Irregular, frontal wind
Cold water for most of the season
Lots of holidaymakers in summer, little room to launch
Easterly winds are offshore and gusty

teriberka-kola.description: Teriberka is a village on the Barents Sea coast, 2–2.5 h from Murmansk, that has become one of Russia's main snowkiting destinations. People ride on the spit at the river mouth, on frozen lakes and in the hilly tundra around Mount Eriveiv and the Verkhne-Teriberka Reservoir. The season runs from late November to April; the best time is March to early April: long days, firm snow and the strongest wind.
teriberka-kola.rating_basis: One of Russia's main snowkiting regions: vast open tundra, frequent strong wind and Arctic scenery; camps are run by big schools (Riders of the Storm, SnowKiteWorld and others); downsides — harsh weather and the polar night
teriberka-kola.waves_note: Snow-covered tundra with hills up to ~300 m, frozen lakes and the Verkhne-Teriberka Reservoir; the spit at the river mouth is a convenient launch
teriberka-kola.hazards: Blizzards and whiteout, frostbite, rocks on wind-scoured slopes, no phone signal in remote areas; distant spots only with a guide
teriberka-kola.gustiness_note: The wind off the sea is strong and frequent, gusty near hills and over terrain; in March it blows ~9 days out of 10 (according to the organisers)
teriberka-kola.crowd_note: Mostly kite-tour groups ride here; the tundra is practically empty
pros: Arctic scenery and the northern lights
Organised kite camps with transfers from Murmansk
cons: Polar night in December–early January
Blizzards close the Murmansk–Teriberka road
Cold and strong wind — good gear is essential
Remote spots with no signal
teriberka-kola.wind_dir: Any direction — open tundra; often strong wind off the Barents Sea

long-bay-providenciales.description: A huge shallow bay with turquoise water on the southeast of Providenciales — the main kite spot of the Turks and Caicos, where all the island's schools are based. At low tide the water is knee- to thigh-deep for kilometres around, with a soft sandy bottom and a steady onshore trade wind — one of the best places in the Caribbean to learn and practise tricks. Advanced riders also ride at Emerald Point.
long-bay-providenciales.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG — 3.8/5 for Providenciales: excellent conditions for learning and freestyle, waist-deep shallows for kilometres and few people; Long Bay's peak season is late November–April
long-bay-providenciales.waves_note: No waves or shorebreak; at low tide the water is mid-thigh deep and you can walk out more than 1.5 km; at high tide (range ~60–70 cm) it's shoulder-deep with moderate chop
long-bay-providenciales.hazards: Occasional rocks and shells on the bottom, wind shadow near the shipwreck; at neighbouring Emerald Point — strong currents in the channel, reef and boats; hurricane season June–November
long-bay-providenciales.gustiness_note: The ocean trade wind is unobstructed and steady; in side-onshore wind there can be wind shadow near the shipwreck
long-bay-providenciales.crowd_note: Busy only at low tide, when the schools are running; the rest of the time there's almost unlimited room
pros: Huge shallows with a soft sandy bottom
cons: A very expensive destination
Deeper and choppier at high tide
September–October — light wind and hurricane season

hua-hin.description: Hua Hin is a royal resort 3–4 hours from Bangkok and one of Thailand's first kite centres: 6 km of sandy beach from the centre to the Khao Takiap headland, with more than ten schools. The northeast monsoon blows in winter, and a steady afternoon sea breeze in spring. A good place to learn, but conditions are more modest than in Pranburi and Mui Ne.
hua-hin.rating_basis: One of Thailand's oldest kite centres (it has hosted PKRA tour stops), with “at least ten schools”, but reviews on Seabreeze mention chop, murky water and an unsteady breeze; the wind is moderate, nothing “wow”
hua-hin.waves_note: An open beach on the gulf: in the northeast monsoon — chop and small wind waves near shore, murkier water; in the spring breeze the water is clearer and the waves small. No flat water
hua-hin.hazards: Jellyfish (November and March–May, especially in SE wind) — wear a wetsuit/rash vest; swimmers, buoys and jet skis; rocks north of the Sofitel hotel and a military zone beyond them — no entry
hua-hin.gustiness_note: November–January: monsoon of 8–20 kn in cycles of 6–10 days, stronger in the morning; February–May: afternoon breeze of 12–20 kn (13:00–17:00); from mid-May to October — gusty offshore SW, not worth riding
hua-hin.crowd_note: A long beach, usually not crowded; swimmers, buoys and jet skis get in the way
hua-hin.region: Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, west coast of the Gulf of Thailand
pros: Close to Bangkok, well-developed resort infrastructure
Two seasons: monsoon November–January and breeze February–April
Gently sloping sandy beach with no reef — easy to learn
cons: Moderate wind (usually 10–20 kn), windless days happen
Chop and murky water in the monsoon
At high tide from November to March the beach almost disappears
Offshore, gusty wind in summer
hua-hin.wind_dir: N–NE in winter (cross-onshore), SE sea breeze in spring (side-onshore); SW in summer — offshore
hua-hin.airport: BKK — Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi), ~3–4 h; HHQ — Hua Hin (few flights)

phuket-nai-yang.description: Nai Yang is a long beach in Sirinat National Park next to Phuket airport. In the southwest monsoon season (May–October) the island's kite schools move here: the wind is side-onshore, there's a lagoon inside the reef and waves on the reef. In winter (November–April) Phuket's kiters ride on the east side — in the Rawai / Chalong lagoon.
phuket-nai-yang.rating_basis: Phuket's main summer (May–October) kite spot; Phuket101 guides recommend it mainly for intermediate and advanced riders; the scale and steadiness of the wind are more modest than at the top monsoon spots
phuket-nai-yang.waves_note: Inside the outer reef — a lagoon with chop and relatively calm water at high tide; waves on the reef and in a strong monsoon, for advanced riders
phuket-nai-yang.hazards: Reef and shallows at low tide, rip currents in the monsoon (red flags), squalls, proximity to the airport runway — ride only in the permitted zone
phuket-nai-yang.gustiness_note: The southwest monsoon is stronger and less predictable than the winter wind on the east of the island; squalls with downpours happen
phuket-nai-yang.crowd_note: Low tourist season — plenty of room on the beach and the water
phuket-nai-yang.region: Phuket, northwest coast (Andaman Sea), by the airport
pros: A summer season, when there's little wind in the Gulf of Thailand
Quiet national park beach, few tourists in the low season
cons: Rainy season: squalls and downpours
Not the best place for complete beginners
Reef bottom and shallows at low tide
Limited choice of schools

pranburi-pak-nam-pran.description: Pak Nam Pran is a 7–10 km sandy beach at the mouth of the Pran River, an hour's drive south of Hua Hin. The headland catches the wind almost year-round: the northeast monsoon in winter, a steady southerly breeze in spring. A quiet place with fishing villages and boutique hotels; several IKO schools, including a KBA branch.
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.rating_basis: Local riders on Seabreeze call Pak Nam Pran a “much better beach” than Hua Hin; it has hosted the IKA TT:R Asian Championship and KTA Freestyle X (March 2017); 12–20 kn wind, a long empty beach
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.waves_note: October–January (NE) — chop and small waves; February–June — smoother water, and by March sandbanks form with patches of flat water (flat for freestyle)
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.hazards: Currents at the river mouth are stronger than on the open beach; no lifeguards on the beach; offshore wind in summer; jellyfish in spring (as along the whole Hua Hin coast)
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.gustiness_note: The winter monsoon is stronger in the morning and dies down by midday; in spring the southerly is lighter but steadier, with thermals boosting it from 12–13:00. The headland strengthens the wind compared with Hua Hin
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.crowd_note: Empty on weekdays; at weekends Thais come from Bangkok — kiters and holidaymakers
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.region: Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, ~30 km south of Hua Hin
pros: Longer season and steadier wind than in Hua Hin
Flat water by the sandbanks in spring
Nearby: a spot at the Pranburi dam (fresh water) and the bays of Khao Kalok and Dolphin Bay
cons: Wind rarely over 20 kn
Little entertainment and infrastructure
July–September — unreliable offshore wind
3.5–4 h from Bangkok
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.wind_dir: NE in winter (cross-onshore), S–SE breeze February–June (side-shore); July–September — often offshore
pranburi-pak-nam-pran.airport: BKK — Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi), ~3.5–4 h; HHQ — Hua Hin, ~40 min

djerba-lagoon.description: A flat, warm island off the coast of Tunisia with all-inclusive hotels and shallow lagoons in the southeast, where you can learn in waist-deep water. The wind is changeable: stronger in spring and autumn, a thermal breeze in summer. A good option for combining a beach holiday with kiting.
djerba-lagoon.rating_basis: Extensive shallow lagoons and warm water in summer, but the wind is lighter and less regular than on the Red Sea; popular with Europeans as a kite destination; rated on general spot descriptions
djerba-lagoon.waves_note: The shallow lagoons in the island's southeast — flat water; on the open beaches in the east (Sidi Mahrez) — chop
djerba-lagoon.hazards: Shallows and seaweed/rocks on the bottom in places, jellyfish in summer
djerba-lagoon.gustiness_note: Mostly a thermal breeze in summer, frontal winds in spring and autumn; less steady than in Egypt
djerba-lagoon.crowd_note: The lagoons are big and uncrowded; moderately busy at the hotel stations
pros: Shallow flat lagoons — easy to learn
Inexpensive hotels, short flight from Europe
cons: Less reliable wind than in Egypt and Morocco
Few kite stations and little information
Heat and lighter wind in summer
djerba-lagoon.wind_dir: E–NE and N, side-shore (depending on the beach)

akyaka-gokova.description: A sandy kite beach by a nature reserve at the very head of Gökova Bay, next to the eco-village of Akyaka. The long, narrow bay acts as a funnel for the daily summer thermal: from June to September there's wind almost every day, and the water is flat and shallow for ~150 m from shore. One of Turkey's most reliable and safest spots for learning.
akyaka-gokova.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: wind on ~75% of days in May and ~99% from June to September, “the perfect place to learn freestyle”, no obstacles or waves; kitejungle — “very steady 15–25 kn wind in the afternoon”
akyaka-gokova.waves_note: Flat, shallow water, no waves or shorebreak; towards the south end of the beach the wind is stronger and light chop appears
akyaka-gokova.hazards: Practically no obstacles; lots of students at the kite beach. Park carefully — the reserve is right next door
akyaka-gokova.gustiness_note: The long bay works as a funnel: light wind from ~9:00, 18–20 kn by midday, holding until evening; a steady thermal with no gusts
akyaka-gokova.crowd_note: Usually uncrowded, but busy at the kite beach because of students — you can move further along the bay
pros: Almost guaranteed wind from June to September
Flat shallow water, onshore — safe for beginners
Warm water and the cosy village of Akyaka with fish restaurants on the Azmak river
cons: The wind rarely exceeds 20–22 kn — not enough for “big” jumps
Calm in the morning, riding in the afternoon
Very hot in July–August
akyaka-gokova.airport: DLM — Dalaman, ~50 min; BJV — Bodrum, ~2 h

alacati-kite-beach.description: Alaçatı is Turkey's best-known wind resort, 1 h from İzmir. Alaçatı Bay is given over to windsurfers (port, Çark), while the kite beaches are on the east side of the bay — about 20 minutes by car around the bay. In summer the northerly Poyraz (Meltemi) blows almost daily and the water is flat, with about 500 m of standing depth near shore. Nearby is the trendy town of Alaçatı with restaurants and boutique hotels.
alacati-kite-beach.rating_basis: Turkey's main wind resort: kite-and-windsurfing-guide — “the perfect place for freestyle and freeride”, a ~500 m standing zone; kitejungle — 181 windy days a year not counting thermals
alacati-kite-beach.waves_note: In northerly wind (Meltemi/Poyraz) the water is flat or lightly choppy; in the southerly Lodos in spring and autumn small, soft waves roll in
alacati-kite-beach.hazards: Lots of students and kites on the water, gusts from the morning Gerens; in southerly wind — waves and being pushed onto the shore
alacati-kite-beach.gustiness_note: The summer Poyraz is 5–7 Bft in the afternoon; the morning northeasterly Gerens can be stronger and gustier
alacati-kite-beach.crowd_note: Kitejungle says “medium”, but in July–August the kite beach has lots of schools and students; windsurfers ride separately, in the western part of the bay
pros: Flat water and a big shallow area — good for learning and freestyle
Well-developed infrastructure, İzmir and a resort town nearby
cons: Crowded in high season
Water cooler than in southern Turkey (upwelling in the Meltemi)
The wind can be gusty in the morning
alacati-kite-beach.wind_dir: N–NNE (Poyraz / Meltemi), side-shore; sometimes the NE “Gerens” in the morning

ayvalik-kite-beach.description: A resort town in the north of the Turkish Aegean, opposite Lesbos. Two spots: Kite Beach with a kite station and restaurant, and the Causeway on the road to Cunda Island — glassy “speed” water in offshore wind. The northerly summer wind blows from about mid-June to mid-September, the most reliable months being July and August. The riding area stretches for more than 5 km.
ayvalik-kite-beach.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG calls Ayvalık “Turkey's secret spot” and the Causeway “one of the best flat-water spots we've found”; Aaron Hadlow and Sam Light have ridden here
ayvalik-kite-beach.waves_note: Flat, shallow, clear water at both spots; no waves or shorebreak
ayvalik-kite-beach.hazards: Offshore wind at the Causeway; the Kite Beach → Causeway downwinder only as an organised trip with locals
ayvalik-kite-beach.gustiness_note: With a light northerly forecast and +28–30 °C heat — a 12 m day; on normal days 7–9 m; up to ~30 kn
ayvalik-kite-beach.crowd_note: According to IKSURFMAG — “really only a few kiters around”
pros: Flat shallow water — from learning to freestyle
Inexpensive, quiet resort with good food
cons: Short season (mid-June to mid-September)
Causeway — offshore wind and no infrastructure
Far from İzmir (~2.5 h)
ayvalik-kite-beach.wind_dir: N (Meltemi), side / side-onshore at Kite Beach; offshore at the Causeway
ayvalik-kite-beach.airport: EDO — Edremit, ~40 min; ADB — İzmir, ~2.5 h

urla-gulbahce.description: Gülbahçe Bay (Çarpan) near Urla is the first kite spot on the way from İzmir to the Çeşme Peninsula, about 30 minutes short of Alaçatı. Shallow, lagoon-like water and the northerly summer wind make it a handy place to learn; on the shore there are several schools with rentals, cafés and showers. There are three launch points: the southwest shore (schools), the east shore (side-shore) and a shallow spit in the north.
urla-gulbahce.rating_basis: The closest kite spot to İzmir, with flat shallow water and several schools (kitejungle); reviews say it's less windy than Alaçatı but easier for learning
urla-gulbahce.waves_note: An enclosed bay: flat water or light chop, no waves; glassy water for speed at the northern spit
urla-gulbahce.hazards: Offshore, gusty wind at the northern spit; lots of students around the schools
urla-gulbahce.gustiness_note: Northerly summer wind plus a daytime thermal; at the northern spit the wind is offshore and gusty
pros: Shallow flat water — easy to learn
Close to İzmir and the airport
cons: Lighter and less steady wind than in Alaçatı
Northern spit — offshore wind, experienced riders only
urla-gulbahce.wind_dir: N (Poyraz / Meltemi), side-shore on the east shore; strong offshore at the northern spit

zanzibar-paje.description: A snow-white beach in southeast Zanzibar with a huge, shallow, reef-protected lagoon. Two seasons: the northerly Kaskazi (Dec–Feb) and the stronger southeasterly Kusi (Jun–Sep). Riding depends entirely on the tide: at low water the inner lagoon dries out and everyone moves to the outer lagoon and the sandbanks.
zanzibar-paje.rating_basis: IKSURFMAG: knee-deep flat lagoons, two wind seasons, warm water, dolphins and turtles; downsides — heavy tide dependence, sea urchins and seaweed farms
zanzibar-paje.waves_note: Inner and outer lagoons — knee-deep flat water (tide-dependent); chop and kickers at high tide; waves on the reef ~1–2 km out
zanzibar-paje.hazards: Sea urchins (booties needed), coral on the reef, seaweed farms, currents at the reef pass, shallows at low tide
