zanzibar-paje.gustiness_note: The monsoon winds are steady; the Kusi is lighter in the morning and builds in the afternoon
zanzibar-paje.crowd_note: Paje is Zanzibar's main kite centre, and the lagoon is busy in season (especially at low tide, when everyone moves to the outer lagoon)
zanzibar-paje.region: East coast of Zanzibar (Unguja), Indian Ocean
pros: Knee-deep flat water — ideal for learning
Dolphins, turtles, beach parties, Stone Town
cons: Riding is tied to the tides
Sea urchins and seaweed farms
Rainy season (April–May) with almost no wind
Crowded in peak season
zanzibar-paje.wind_dir: Kaskazi — NE (Dec–Feb), Kusi — SE (Jun–Sep); side-shore / side-onshore

cape-hatteras-waves.description: The Outer Banks are a narrow chain of barrier islands between the Atlantic and Pamlico Sound. On the sound side there are endless waist-deep flat-water shallows, ideal for learning and freestyle; on the ocean side, waves. The centre of the kite scene is the village of Waves, with the REAL Watersports kite resort and the Real Slick park. The best months are May and September–October; winter is windy but cold.
cape-hatteras-waves.rating_basis: The main kite resort on the US East Coast: windy months all year round, the huge shallow flat-water lagoon of Pamlico Sound; kickers and sliders at Real Slick (REAL Watersports)
cape-hatteras-waves.waves_note: On the Pamlico Sound side — a huge shallow area with flat water and chop, no shorebreak; waves on the island's ocean side
cape-hatteras-waves.hazards: Hurricanes and storms (June–November), thunderstorms as fronts pass through, jellyfish and crabs in the shallows in summer, sliders and kickers in the kite park
cape-hatteras-waves.gustiness_note: An open barrier island: the wind is steady (the IKSURFMAG author — “the most consistent wind in a long time”); the direction changes with the season and the fronts
cape-hatteras-waves.crowd_note: Busy around the kite centres in spring and autumn, but there are enough shallows for everyone; most water access is via private paths
pros: Wind at any time of year
cons: Cold water and air in winter
Lighter wind and heat in summer
A long drive from the airports (~2–2.5 h from Norfolk)
cape-hatteras-waves.wind_dir: SW in summer, NE/N in autumn and spring; usually side-shore at Real Slick
cape-hatteras-waves.airport: ORF — Norfolk, ~2–2.5 h; MQI — Dare County (general aviation), ~30 min

corpus-christi-packery-channel.description: Packery Channel is a shallow spot on the Laguna Madre side of North Padre Island: knee- to waist-deep flat water and a grassy bottom. Corpus Christi is famous for its constant summer southeasterly; the main season is May–September, but you can ride year-round. Around it are a dozen other spots (Wildcat, North Beach, Oso Bay, Fish Pass).
corpus-christi-packery-channel.rating_basis: Local riders call Corpus Christi the “holy grail” for having the most rideable days in the US; kiteboarding.com: SE 17–21 mph all summer
corpus-christi-packery-channel.waves_note: Knee- to waist-deep flat water; sometimes waves on the ocean side by the jetty
corpus-christi-packery-channel.hazards: Oyster shells (booties a must), the boat channel in the canal, seaweed; on the ocean side — stay 200 yards from the north jetty
corpus-christi-packery-channel.gustiness_note: The summer SE is steady (thermals over land strengthen the flow); the frontal northerly in winter is gusty
corpus-christi-packery-channel.crowd_note: Lots of spots within 30 min — kiters are spread out
pros: Shallow flat water, good for learning
cons: Cold fronts in winter, gusty N and cool water
Booties needed because of oyster shells
Kiting is banned in Padre Island National Seashore (Bird Island Basin)
corpus-christi-packery-channel.wind_dir: SE in summer (side-onshore), N with cold fronts in winter

hood-river.description: A small town in the Columbia River Gorge — North America's summer capital of kiting and windsurfing. Wind from the Pacific accelerates through the gorge and blows almost every day from May to September. The main launches are the sandbar at the mouth of the Hood River and the Event Site; the water is dense chop and river swell running against the current. Fresh water, the Mount Hood volcano on the horizon and plenty to do on windless days.
hood-river.rating_basis: North America's cult river spot: strong wind almost every summer day (usually 18–25 mph, IKSURFMAG), lots of spots along the gorge (Stevenson, Rufus) and a well-developed kite culture
hood-river.waves_note: Dense river chop at the Event Site, flat water downstream behind the sandbar; in strong wind against the current a river swell builds (bigger and cleaner at Rufus, 45 miles east)
hood-river.hazards: Strong river current (sweeps you downstream if you crash), a shipping channel with barges, cold water in spring and autumn, slippery rocks at the Stevenson and Rufus launches
hood-river.gustiness_note: The summer wind “blows through” the Columbia Gorge from the west: strong and often gusty; steadier at Stevenson
hood-river.crowd_note: The Event Site is the busiest launch in the gorge — crowded in summer, with hotels fully booked at weekends; quieter upstream
pros: Fresh water, no salt or jellyfish
Lots of spots along the gorge
Great infrastructure and things to do on windless days
cons: The water is cool even in summer — wetsuit needed
Gusty and crowded
Strong current and barges — not for complete beginners

maui-kanaha-kite-beach.description: Kanaha Beach next to Kahului airport is the heart of Maui's kite scene, where many tricks and brands were born. The trade wind blows almost every day from spring to autumn; there's chop near shore and quality waves on the outer reef, big in winter. Beginners are taught at neighbouring Teach Beach; the kite zones are restricted because of the nearby airport.
maui-kanaha-kite-beach.rating_basis: The birthplace of modern kitesurfing and one of the world's wave meccas: leading brands and riders are based at Kite Beach (Naish Beach); IKSURFMAG — windy months March–October, trade wind 15–25 mph
maui-kanaha-kite-beach.waves_note: Chop and a small shorebreak near shore, lines of waves on the outer reef, overhead in winter swells; at Kihei in the south — waves in a south swell
maui-kanaha-kite-beach.hazards: Shallow reef (dangerous if you fall), shorebreak, powerful swell in winter; sharks and turtles possible; respect the kite zone boundaries near the airport
maui-kanaha-kite-beach.gustiness_note: The trade wind blows a steady 15–25 mph on most days from spring to autumn; in winter the wind is less reliable, with occasional southerly “Kona” winds
maui-kanaha-kite-beach.crowd_note: Kite Beach is the island's main spot, and the reef gets crowded in good wind; lessons are held separately at Teach Beach
cons: Reef and waves — not a place for beginners
Expensive (accommodation, car)
Restricted riding zones because of the airport

el-yaque.description: A village in the south of Margarita Island, known for decades as the world capital of windsurfing, and later of kiting. A huge shallow bay with chop and a side-shore trade wind suits both beginners and freestylers, and boat trips to Coche Island offer perfectly flat water. The resort is half-empty these days — fewer people, but weaker infrastructure; schools arrange transfers and trips to Araya and La Restinga.
el-yaque.rating_basis: A legendary Caribbean windsurf/kite spot with shallow warm water and wind “almost all year round” (IKSURFMAG); today almost free of crowds because of the situation in Venezuela; Russian-language roundups mention Venezuela as the best winter destination
el-yaque.waves_note: No waves at El Yaque — light chop, waist-deep far from shore; perfectly flat water at Coche Island (20 min by boat or a 15 km downwinder); waves at La Restinga
el-yaque.hazards: Gusty wind in the afternoon, offshore wind at Coche (the school boat provides backup), shells on La Restinga beach; safety: don't rent a car, use school transfers, check foreign ministry travel advice
el-yaque.gustiness_note: Trade wind almost every day, but it can be gusty after midday; at Coche the wind is offshore and picks up by 10 a.m.
el-yaque.crowd_note: IKSURFMAG: “you won't find crowded spots these days”; windsurfers and kiters share the beach
pros: Shallow warm water far from shore
Wind almost every day from February to July
Trips to the flat water of Coche and Araya
cons: Complicated logistics: no direct international flights (via Caracas)
The political and crime situation in Venezuela
Gusty after midday
el-yaque.airport: PMV — Porlamar (Margarita), ~40 min; international flights via CCS Caracas

mui-ne.description: Mui Ne is Vietnam's main kite resort and one of the most Russian-speaking kite places in Asia: dozens of schools along Ham Tien beach, including some with Russian instructors (MKS, KiteFamily, KITENAM and others). From November to March a strong northeast monsoon blows, boosted by thermals. Besides the main beach there's Malibu (waves), Harbour Wall (flat water), Suối Nước and Turtle Island; 3–4 h to the north is the Phan Rang lagoon.
mui-ne.rating_basis: One of Asia's best-known kite resorts (Figaro Nautisme names Mui Ne among Asia's top destinations); a steady monsoon November–March, strong wind and waves, lots of schools; downsides — crowding and shorebreak at high tide
mui-ne.waves_note: On the main beach — shorebreak and 1–2 m waves, up to 2–3 m in strong wind in December–February; Malibu — waves and onshore wind; by the Harbour Wall and at Secret Spot — the only flat water in the area
mui-ne.hazards: Strong shorebreak at high tide, erosion and a narrow beach in the northern part of Rang Beach, a rocky headland by Ganh Beach and at the Cemetery spot, crowds and people ignoring right-of-way rules, jellyfish (low risk), strong sun
mui-ne.gustiness_note: The monsoon is boosted by thermals: 10–15 kn in the morning, 20–25 by midday, 25–30+ in the afternoon; gusty at Harbour Wall after 13:00 and at Turtle Island
mui-ne.crowd_note: Crowded on the main beach in December–January, sometimes 30–40 kites on a single stretch; Suối Nước and Malibu are quieter
pros: Lots of schools, including Russian-speaking ones
Warm water year-round, cheap accommodation and food
Several spots for every style: waves, flat water, ~15 km downwinders
cons: Shorebreak and a narrow beach at high tide — a tricky launch for beginners
Crowded on the main beach in peak season
The wind in December–February is often 25–30+ kn — hard for beginners
Litter on some beaches (Malibu, Harbour Wall)
mui-ne.airport: SGN — Ho Chi Minh City, ~4–5 h by car (also CXR — Cam Ranh, ~4 h)

phan-rang-my-hoa.description: My Hoa lagoon by the village of My Tan is the main kite spot in Ninh Thuan Province and the windiest place in Vietnam. An outer reef about 1 km offshore breaks the waves: inside there's shallow flat water for learning, freestyle and speed, and outside the reef there are waves. A small kite village with several schools and kite hotels has grown up around the lagoon; many people come here on camps from Mui Ne.
phan-rang-my-hoa.rating_basis: Described as having stronger, steadier wind than Mui Ne, with a flat lagoon behind the reef; Phan Rang Kite Center — 4.8 on Google (344 reviews) and 5.0 on Tripadvisor; it hosted a Kiteboard Tour Asia event (2016, ~100 riders)
phan-rang-my-hoa.waves_note: Inside the lagoon, sheltered by a reef about 1 km from shore — flat water and light chop; outside the reef — waves for wave riding (experienced riders only). In summer the main spot is Ninh Chu Bay, with flat shallow water
phan-rang-my-hoa.hazards: Coral rubble, sharp shells and rocks at low tide (booties needed), a sudden drop-off at the edge of the bank, the reef and waves beyond it, rapidly strengthening afternoon wind; typhoons possible in May
phan-rang-my-hoa.gustiness_note: One of the windiest areas in Vietnam: the monsoon is boosted by the mountains, averaging ~20–25 kn in season, rarely below 15, sometimes up to 35–40; steadier than in Mui Ne
phan-rang-my-hoa.crowd_note: Much less crowded than Mui Ne: 10–20 riders on a good day, up to a few dozen kites over the lagoon in peak season
phan-rang-my-hoa.region: Ninh Thuan Province (My Tan / Ninh Hai), ~20 km northeast of Phan Rang
pros: Strong, steady monsoon, steadier wind than in Mui Ne
Flat shallow water in the lagoon
Few people compared with Mui Ne
Accommodation 50 m from the launch, Cam Ranh airport ~1 h away
cons: Heavily tide-dependent: coral and rocks are exposed at low tide
Wind often 25+ kn — beginners are better off in the morning
Little infrastructure or entertainment beyond kiting
Small choice of rental gear
phan-rang-my-hoa.wind_dir: N–NE (northeast monsoon), side / side-onshore; S–SSE at Ninh Chu in summer

cape-town-bloubergstrand.description: The Blouberg–Table View coast north of Cape Town, with views of Table Mountain, is a mecca for big air and wave riding. A strong southeasterly blows almost daily from November to March, the water is cold (13–15 °C), and there's a choice of beaches: from the relatively flat Dolphin Beach to the waves of Sunset and Calmers. A great city, wine and nature for windless days.
cape-town-bloubergstrand.rating_basis: One of the world's top destinations for big air and waves: IKSURFMAG — 20–40 knots ~5 days a week from December to February, a dozen beaches along the coast, downwinders with views of Table Mountain
cape-town-bloubergstrand.waves_note: Chop and kickers almost everywhere; Dolphin Beach has the flattest water at high tide; Sunset Beach and Calmers — clean waves, big in a swell; strong shorebreak at Doodles
cape-town-bloubergstrand.hazards: Cold water, strong gusts, shorebreak (Doodles, Sunset), rocks at Big Bay and north of Calmers, currents; theft from cars in car parks
cape-town-bloubergstrand.gustiness_note: The southeasterly “Cape Doctor” is strong and regular but comes in surges near Table Mountain; it picks up by ~10:00 and peaks by 16:00
cape-town-bloubergstrand.crowd_note: In December–February the whole kite world descends; crowded at Big Bay, Dolphin Beach (school groups) and Calmers; November and March are quieter
pros: Strong, regular wind in the southern summer
Wide choice of beaches and waves
cons: Cold water — 4/3–5/4 mm wetsuit
The wind is often too strong for beginners
Crime: don't leave things in the car, be careful in the evening
Long-haul flight

langebaan-lagoon.description: A long (≈15 km) enclosed lagoon on South Africa's West Coast, part of West Coast National Park. The southerly summer wind blows along the shore over flat or slightly rippled water — a great place for learning and freestyle when Cape Town is too windy or too wavy. The water is noticeably warmer than in Table Bay.
langebaan-lagoon.rating_basis: The Western Cape's main flat-water spot: a long shallow lagoon in West Coast National Park where freestylers train (mentioned in IKSURFMAG's Cape Town guide); the water is warmer than at Table View
langebaan-lagoon.waves_note: The lagoon is closed off from the ocean — no waves; flat in the shallow zones, chop in strong wind
langebaan-lagoon.hazards: Currents at the lagoon outlet when the tide turns, nature conservation zones (part of the water is closed), strong sun
langebaan-lagoon.gustiness_note: The same southerly summer wind as in Cape Town, but over flat terrain — steadier and without the “surges” off the mountains
langebaan-lagoon.crowd_note: Shark Bay is busy in December–January, but the lagoon is long — you can move along the shore
langebaan-lagoon.region: Western Cape, West Coast, ~1.5 h north of Cape Town
pros: Steadier wind than in Cape Town
Warmer water than at the ocean beaches
cons: 1.5 h from Cape Town — car needed
Little entertainment in the town
In winter (May–September) the wind is light and it's cold
